You're pulling the gun down and left when you pull the trigger. Exhale when you pull the trigger and use only the tip of your finger to pull the trigger.

Are you shooting lefty or right handed?
Slow down your trigger pull, make sure it is a smooth motion while exhaling. For right handed shooters a jerky trigger pull typically causes the lower left grouping.
thank you. it's weird - when I've tried dry firing at home I move it upwards if anything, but it does feel like I do something different on the range.

More than likely on range you are anticipating the shot, pretty normal for new or irregular shooters. Once you find a good breathing/trigger rhythm your groupings will be great. They already look pretty good.

Thank you. Last time I went I tried shooting just one live round from the chamber, no mag, and then dry firing and I definitely noticed more movement during the dry fire. Not complaining about needing more practice, having a great time learning to shoot :)

If it moves at all when you are dry firing then keep practicing. That isn't the hardest part but it is the first step. Once you can do that you have to learn to be completely unphased by the weapon firing in your hands and teach yourself to do the exact same motion as dry firing. Breath control and sight picture are important but they would result in scatted groups on center, not tight groups off center.

I'm gonna assume it's been said, but yes. Stop flinching. Get some snap caps and go through at least a few hundred dry fire drills (it is fine to do these in your home) concentrating on breath control, sight alignment, and trigger control. It may also take several thousand rounds of live fire shooting to get completely comfortable pulling the trigger. Getting some in person professional instruction will do more for you than you can imagine.
